name: Learn: Debugging & Observability
objective: CKAD › Application Observability and Maintenance (15%). Goal: diagnose and fix failing workloads using kubectl logs, describe, and events — CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff, Pending (unschedulable), reading container stdout, and a failing readiness probe.
description: The core CKAD debugging loop: read logs, describe, and events to find why a workload is unhealthy, then fix it. Covers CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff, a Pending pod, retrieving a line from container logs, and a broken readiness probe.

questions.title: Fix a CrashLoopBackOff pod (read logs)
questions.teach:
A pod in **CrashLoopBackOff** starts, exits, and Kubernetes restarts it on a growing back-off. The state just means *restarting repeatedly* — use **`kubectl logs <pod>`** to find the real cause, then fix the command. A pod's `command` can't be patched in place, so delete and recreate it.

**Gotcha:** on a fast-crashing pod the current logs are often empty — read the last crashed instance with **`kubectl logs <pod> --previous`** (`-p`).
questions.prompt:
Pod `crasher` in namespace `ckad-observability` is in CrashLoopBackOff — its command is wrong. Inspect it, then fix it so it runs a long-lived process (image `busybox:1.36`, e.g. `sleep 3600`).

Target: pod `crasher` is `Running` and `Ready` (recreate it — you can't patch a pod's command in place).
questions.hint: `kubectl logs crasher -n ckad-observability` (or `--previous`) shows the error. Delete and recreate: `kubectl delete pod crasher -n ckad-observability` then `kubectl run crasher -n ckad-observability --image=busybox:1.36 --command -- sleep 3600`.
questions.solution:
kubectl logs crasher -n ckad-observability --previous
kubectl describe pod crasher -n ckad-observability
kubectl delete pod crasher -n ckad-observability
kubectl run crasher -n ckad-observability --image=busybox:1.36 --command -- sleep 3600
kubectl get pod crasher -n ckad-observability   # Running, Ready

verification.description: pod 'crasher' is Running and Ready (no CrashLoop)

questions.title: Fix an ImagePullBackOff Deployment (describe + events)
questions.teach:
**ImagePullBackOff** means the node can't pull the image. `kubectl logs` is useless here — the container never started — so diagnose with **`kubectl describe pod`** / **`kubectl get events`**, which name the exact bad reference (e.g. `manifest ... not found` for a wrong tag). Fix a Deployment with **`kubectl set image deploy/<name> <container>=<image>`**, which triggers a rollout.

**Gotcha:** `set image` takes the **container name**, not the pod name — `deploy/web web=...`; get it from `describe` or the spec.
questions.prompt:
Deployment `web` in `ckad-observability` is stuck — its pods are in ImagePullBackOff because of a bad image tag. Diagnose with describe/events, then update it to a pullable image (`nginx:1.25-alpine`).

Target: Deployment `web` has its pods `Running` (all replicas available).
questions.hint: `kubectl describe deploy web -n ckad-observability` and `kubectl get events -n ckad-observability` show the failed image. Fix with `kubectl set image deploy/web web=nginx:1.25-alpine -n ckad-observability`.
questions.solution:
kubectl get pods -n ckad-observability
kubectl describe pod -l app=web -n ckad-observability | grep -A3 Events
kubectl set image deploy/web web=nginx:1.25-alpine -n ckad-observability
kubectl rollout status deploy/web -n ckad-observability

questions.title: Fix a Pending pod (unschedulable resources)
questions.teach:
A pod stays **Pending** when the scheduler can't bind it to a node. **`kubectl describe pod`** → Events shows a **`FailedScheduling`** reason; `Insufficient cpu` means the pod's `resources.requests` exceeds every node's free allocatable. Lower the request (`100m` = 0.1 core) so it fits. You can't patch a pod's `resources` in place — delete and recreate.

**Gotcha:** scheduling weighs **requests**, not limits — a huge limit alone won't block it, but a huge request will.
questions.prompt:
Pod `bigask` in `ckad-observability` is stuck `Pending` — it requests an impossible amount of CPU. Diagnose with describe, then recreate it (image `busybox:1.36`, `sleep 3600`) with a schedulable CPU request such as `100m`.

Target: pod `bigask` is `Running`.
questions.hint: `kubectl describe pod bigask -n ckad-observability` → Events show `FailedScheduling ... Insufficient cpu`. Delete it, then recreate with a small request, e.g. `kubectl run bigask -n ckad-observability --image=busybox:1.36 --overrides='{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"bigask","image":"busybox:1.36","command":["sleep","3600"],"resources":{"requests":{"cpu":"100m"}}}]}}'`.
questions.solution:
kubectl describe pod bigask -n ckad-observability | grep -A5 Events
kubectl delete pod bigask -n ckad-observability
kubectl run bigask -n ckad-observability --image=busybox:1.36 --overrides='{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"bigask","image":"busybox:1.36","command":["sleep","3600"],"resources":{"requests":{"cpu":"100m"}}}]}}'
kubectl get pod bigask -n ckad-observability   # Running

questions.title: Capture a line from container logs
questions.teach:
**`kubectl logs <pod>`** returns whatever the container wrote to **stdout/stderr** — run a pod that prints a line, then read it back. Store the captured value in a ConfigMap with **`kubectl create configmap <name> --from-literal=key=value`**.

**Gotcha:** `logs` only shows stdout/stderr — an app that writes to a file *inside* the container shows nothing.
questions.prompt:
Run a pod `logger` (image `busybox:1.36`) whose command prints the exact line `MARKER=ckad-obs-42` to stdout and then stays running (e.g. `echo MARKER=ckad-obs-42; sleep 3600`). Read it back with `kubectl logs`, then create a ConfigMap `captured` in `ckad-observability` with key `token` set to that value `ckad-obs-42`.

Target: pod `logger` logged `MARKER=ckad-obs-42` AND ConfigMap `captured` has `token=ckad-obs-42`.
questions.hint: `kubectl run logger -n ckad-observability --image=busybox:1.36 --command -- sh -c 'echo MARKER=ckad-obs-42; sleep 3600'`, then `kubectl logs logger -n ckad-observability`, then `kubectl create configmap captured -n ckad-observability --from-literal=token=ckad-obs-42`.
questions.solution:
kubectl run logger -n ckad-observability --image=busybox:1.36 --command -- sh -c 'echo MARKER=ckad-obs-42; sleep 3600'
kubectl logs logger -n ckad-observability   # MARKER=ckad-obs-42
kubectl create configmap captured -n ckad-observability --from-literal=token=ckad-obs-42

verification.description: logger printed the marker AND configmap 'captured' holds token=ckad-obs-42

questions.title: Fix a failing readiness probe
questions.teach:
A **readiness probe** gates traffic: until it passes the pod is `Running` but **not Ready**, so it's pulled from Service endpoints and doesn't count toward `availableReplicas`. A wrong `httpGet` path never succeeds — `kubectl describe pod` shows `Readiness probe failed: ... statuscode: 404`. Fix the path on the **controller template** (`kubectl edit`/`patch deploy`), not the pod.

**Gotcha:** you can't patch a pod's probe in place — edit the Deployment so a new ReplicaSet picks it up.
questions.prompt:
Deployment `ready-web` in `ckad-observability` runs nginx but stays at 0 available — its readiness probe does an httpGet on the wrong path `/healthz` (nginx returns 404). Fix the probe path to `/` so the pods pass readiness.

Target: Deployment `ready-web` reports `availableReplicas` ≥ 1.
questions.hint: `kubectl describe pod -l app=ready-web -n ckad-observability` shows the 404. Patch the path: `kubectl patch deploy ready-web -n ckad-observability --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/readinessProbe/httpGet/path","value":"/"}]'` (or `kubectl edit`).
questions.solution:
kubectl describe pod -l app=ready-web -n ckad-observability | grep -i readiness
kubectl patch deploy ready-web -n ckad-observability --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/readinessProbe/httpGet/path","value":"/"}]'
kubectl rollout status deploy/ready-web -n ckad-observability

questions.title: Debug a running pod with an ephemeral container
questions.teach:
`kubectl debug` attaches an **ephemeral container** to a *running* pod — a temporary debug container sharing the pod's namespaces, so you can troubleshoot an image that has no shell/tools without restarting it. `--target=<container>` shares that container's process namespace.

**Gotcha:** ephemeral containers can't be removed or restarted — they're for live debugging, not permanent sidecars.
questions.prompt:
Pod `blackbox` in `ckad-observability` is running but you can't `exec` into its container `app`. Use `kubectl debug` to add an **ephemeral debug container** (image `busybox:1.36`) targeting container `app`.

Target: pod `blackbox` has an ephemeral container using image `busybox:1.36`.
questions.hint: `kubectl debug -it blackbox -n ckad-observability --image=busybox:1.36 --target=app -- sh` — the ephemeral container stays recorded on the pod even after you exit.
questions.solution:
kubectl debug -it blackbox -n ckad-observability --image=busybox:1.36 --target=app -- sh
# exit the shell; the ephemeral container remains on the pod
kubectl get pod blackbox -n ckad-observability -o jsonpath='{.spec.ephemeralContainers[*].image}'

verification.description: pod 'blackbox' has an ephemeral debug container (busybox:1.36)
